Fit the model at several classifier thresholds

Source: R/fp_threshold_sweep.R
fp_threshold_sweep.Rd

The threshold at which a confidence score counts as a detection trades false positives against missed detections, and it can change the estimated environmental effects (Piatti et al. 2026). This function builds the automated occasions at each threshold with fp_aggregate(), fits the same model to each, and collects the estimates, so that their sensitivity to the threshold can be seen at once.

Usage

fp_threshold_sweep(
  occasions,
  detections,
  thresholds = c("MaxF1", "MaxPrecision"),
  sites,
  verified = NULL,
  site = "site",
  by = "file",
  species = NULL,
  recorder = NULL,
  occ = ~1,
  det = ~1,
  fp = ~1,
  random_recorder = !is.null(recorder),
  prob = 0.95,
  validation = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'fp_threshold_sweep'
plot(x, parameters = NULL, ...)

Arguments

occasions, detections, by, species

Passed to fp_aggregate().

thresholds

Numeric confidence thresholds in [0, 1], or names "MaxF1" and/or "MaxPrecision" to derive thresholds from validation. Defaults to both named methods. Each distinct threshold is fitted once.

sites, verified, site, recorder

Passed to fp_data(); site must also be a column of occasions.

occ, det, fp, random_recorder

Passed to fp_occu().

prob

Width of the credible intervals in the summary.

validation

Optional reviewed clips, as returned by fp_read_validation(), with numeric confidence in [0, 1] and logical (or binary 0/1) verdict. Required for named thresholds. Rows with missing scores or verdicts are dropped with a warning. When species is supplied, validation is filtered by species_code or common_name.

...

Further arguments for fp_occu(), such as chains, threads_per_chain, or seed.

x

An fp_threshold_sweep object.

parameters

Parameters to plot; by default the occupancy slopes and p10_bar.

Value

A data frame of class fp_threshold_sweep with one row per threshold and parameter: the threshold, the share of occasions that are detections, the parameter, its posterior mean and interval, and the number of divergent transitions and largest R-hat of the fit. plot() draws the estimates against the threshold. For named thresholds, attributes threshold_selection and validation_metrics contain the selected methods and the metrics at every candidate threshold, respectively (columns threshold, tp, fp, fn, precision, recall, f1).

Details

Named methods evaluate every distinct validation score, counting scores at or above the threshold as positive. Precision is TP / (TP + FP), recall is TP / (TP + FN), and F1 is 2 TP / (2 TP + FP + FN). The candidates are the observed scores, so each predicts at least one positive. At least one reviewed positive is required. The selected threshold is a score of the validation table, applied with >= to detections; if the validation file stores rounded scores, the clips at the cutoff can fall on the other side. Ties are resolved by greater recall, then the smaller threshold. Recall and F1 refer to positives in the supplied validation set: clips missed by the classifier or excluded by an earlier score cutoff are not represented. Use a representative validation sample for the target species. Validation selects thresholds only; it is not passed as confirmation data to fp_aggregate().

References

Piatti, L., de Sousa, D. L. H., Oliveira, B. S., de Melo, A. V., Sugai, L. S. M., & Provete, D. B. (2026). Methodological choices influence ecological inference in passive acoustic monitoring of a Neotropical nightjar. Journal of Avian Biology, in press.

See also

fp_aggregate()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# occasions: one row per one-minute recording, with site_night and covariates
sweep <- fp_threshold_sweep(occasions, detections, thresholds = c(0.1, 0.4, 0.7),
                            sites = nights, verified = verified,
                            site = "site_night", occ = ~ temp + rh, fp = ~ 1,
                            random_recorder = FALSE)
plot(sweep)
# Derive both thresholds from reviewed classifier clips:
reviews <- fp_read_validation("validation_by_clip.csv")
selected <- fp_threshold_sweep(occasions, detections, sites = nights,
                               site = "site_night", validation = reviews,
                               random_recorder = FALSE)
attr(selected, "threshold_selection")
} # }
